originalTitle: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
summary: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare "whether AI has been used in their work," the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform. content: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare “whether AI has been used in their work,” the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform. “One of the most consistent concerns we’ve heard is that it’s not clearly disclosed when AI has been used to create a mod,” according to the post from site owner Victor “Foledinho” Folmann. “We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognise that there’s a lot more we can do to make that information more accessible and clear for you all.” Any mods tagged as “AI-assisted” will also be required to include “a public explanation of how and where AI was used.” AI tags will also be “more prominent” on mod pages. Folmann says Nexus Mods is “pro-human creativity” but “won’t introduce an outright ban on AI-generated mods.” As for why that is: > The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable. An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use. We’d prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform. Folmann notes that Nexus Mods won’t use mods to train AI and “will not sell or license them to anyone doing so.” However, the site is working on “clearer control” over how mods can be reused on others and strengthening attribution for when “a mod uses another Mod Author’s mod with the appropriate permissions.” Nexus Mods is also making changes to the Recently Added section of the site to address a problem of mod authors uploading many mods at once, which makes other mods fall down down the page. “This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up,” Folmann says. The changes include trying limits on how many mods from one author are shown at a time and “tighter restrictions” on uploads from new accounts. The platform is also launching controls to hide AI-generated content in game pages and on the homepage, and “next up,” in search. Nexus Mods’ full AI policy is here, and mod authors have 60 days to update their existing mods to meet the requirements. The 60-day grace period ends on January 2nd, and after that time, the site will begin enforcing the rules.

chineseContent: PC 游戏模组存储库 Nexus Mods 在上传新模组时强制披​​露有关人工智能的信息，这意味着模组作者必须声明“是否在他们的工作中使用了人工智能”，该网站今天宣布，这是该平台上有关人工智能生成内容的重要帖子的一部分。网站所有者 Victor “Foledinho” Folmann 在帖子中表示：“我们听到的最一致的担忧之一是，没有明确披露何时使用人工智能来创建模组。” “我们已经有了人工智能生成和人工智能辅助模组的标签，但我们认识到，我们可以做更多的事情来让大家更容易获取和清晰地获取这些信息。”任何标记为“人工智能辅助”的模组还需要包含“关于如何以及在何处使用人工智能的公开解释”。 AI 标签也将在模组页面上“更加突出”。 Folmann 表示 Nexus Mods 是“有利于人类创造力”，但“不会彻底禁止人工智能生成的 mods”。至于为什么会这样： > 答案很简单：目前从脚本自动完成到生成纹理、声音和完整资产，人工智能已经贯穿整个创作过程，可接受和不可接受之间很难划清界限。彻底的禁令不会将人工智能从改装过程中消除，但会阻止人们提及它的使用。我们更喜欢相反的情况；它应该是公开的，有明确的标签，并根据我们可以在我们的平台上实施的规则进行监管。 Folmann 指出，Nexus Mods 不会使用 mod 来训练 AI，并且“不会将它们出售或授权给任何这样做的人。”然而，该网站正在致力于“更清晰地控制”如何在其他人身上重复使用模组，并加强对“某个模组使用具有适当权限的另一个模组作者的模组”的归属。 Nexus Mods 是
